explanations.explanation: Yes, friend. Luke says He "went up on a mountain to pray." (Luke 9:28) And look what happens next: while He is praying, His face changes and His clothes turn radiantly white (Luke 9:29). I'd say that's a prayer meeting nobody could ever top.

Fasting is a real thing in the Bible, but it isn't what this verse says. Luke tells us Jesus "went up on a mountain to pray." (Luke 9:28) Not a word about skipping meals up there. I like to keep my eyes on what the verse actually says, even when my stomach has opinions.

A mountain does sound like a nice spot for a nap, friend. But Luke says He went up "to pray." (Luke 9:28) The only ones who end up sleeping are Peter and his companions (Luke 9:32). Jesus is the one praying while the others doze.

That's it, baker. They "spoke about His departure, which He was about to accomplish at Jerusalem." (Luke 9:31) Moses, Israel's leader, and Elijah, the prophet, show up in glory, and that is the topic. I think that's a mighty big conversation to walk in on.

I get why this one is tempting, friend. Moses, Israel's leader, is the one who received the law at Sinai. But Luke says they spoke about "His departure, which He was about to accomplish at Jerusalem." (Luke 9:31) Same visitor, different topic.

Elijah, the prophet, is the one tied to Mount Carmel, so I see the thinking. But Luke never says they talked about that. He says they spoke about "His departure, which He was about to accomplish at Jerusalem." (Luke 9:31) Sometimes the famous story is not the one on the table.

Not quite, baker. Luke says that when they awoke, "they saw Jesus' glory and the two men standing with Him." (Luke 9:32) So Moses and Elijah are still right there when the three wake up. They didn't sleep through the whole thing, thank goodness.

Right, friend. When they woke up, "they saw Jesus' glory and the two men standing with Him." (Luke 9:32) Moses and Elijah haven't left yet. Peter speaks up as they are leaving (Luke 9:33), so the three woke up just in time.

Yes, friend. Peter says, "Let us put up three shelters—one for You, one for Moses, and one for Elijah." (Luke 9:33) Three shelters, three names. I think he is just so happy to be there that he wants to stay put.

Altars show up all over the Bible, so it's a fair guess. But Peter's words are, "Let us put up three shelters." (Luke 9:33) A shelter is a place to stay, not a place for an offering. Close, friend, but the verse says shelters.

Towers would have been a big project, baker. Peter's actual idea is smaller: "Let us put up three shelters." (Luke 9:33) One for Jesus, one for Moses and one for Elijah. Nobody is asking for a skyline.

explanations.answer: He did not know what he was saying
explanations.explanation: That's the note, friend. Luke adds in parentheses, "(He did not know what he was saying.)" (Luke 9:33) I've said a few things in my day that deserved a note like that. Peter just got his written down in the Bible.

explanations.answer: He had learned it from Moses
explanations.explanation: Moses is on the mountain, so I see how it crossed your mind. But Luke says nothing about Peter learning this idea from anyone. The note says, "He did not know what he was saying." (Luke 9:33) Peter came up with it on the spot.

explanations.answer: He had been planning it for days
explanations.explanation: Not this time, baker. The shelters come up as Moses and Elijah are leaving (Luke 9:33), and Luke never says Peter planned a thing. The note is, "He did not know what he was saying." That sounds like words that just came out of him, not a plan in a folder.

Yes, friend. The voice says, "This is My Son, whom I have chosen. Listen to Him!" (Luke 9:35) Peter was still talking when the cloud came, and now the command is to listen. I'd say that's a pretty clear one.

I see the connection, since shelters were Peter's idea. But the voice never asks for one. It says, "This is My Son, whom I have chosen. Listen to Him!" (Luke 9:35) The command is about listening, not building.
Peter did say it was good to be there (Luke 9:33), so staying feels natural. But that is not what the voice says. It says, "Listen to Him!" (Luke 9:35) There's no word about staying put, friend.
That's right, baker. Luke says, "After the voice had spoken, only Jesus was present with them." (Luke 9:36) Moses and Elijah are no longer standing there. Just Jesus with the three of them.

Moses was there on the mountain, but not at the end. Luke says, "After the voice had spoken, only Jesus was present with them." (Luke 9:36) Moses, Israel's leader, is no longer in the picture. Only Jesus is left.

Elijah, the prophet, did show up earlier, so I see why he came to mind. But after the voice spoke, "only Jesus was present with them." (Luke 9:36) That word "only" leaves no room for anyone else, friend.

Not quite, friend. Luke says, "The disciples kept this to themselves, and in those days they did not tell anyone what they had seen." (Luke 9:36) That is a lot to hold in. I'd be about ready to burst.

Right, baker. The text says they "kept this to themselves, and in those days they did not tell anyone what they had seen." (Luke 9:36) A glowing Jesus, Moses and Elijah, a cloud and a voice, and they stayed quiet. I couldn't have done it.
